---
title: "About This Guide"
---

**TinyTorch** is a build-it-yourself educational deep learning framework and curriculum. This **TinyTorch Lab Guide** collects the orientation, quick-start, module-by-module implementation exercises, and historical milestone projects into a single portable reference for offline reading, lab work, and print study.

## Two Pillars: Lab Guide and Textbook

TinyTorch is organized into two complementary pillars:

1. **The TinyTorch Lab Guide (This Document)**
   The hands-on workbook and student implementation manual. Each chapter guides you through building a specific subsystem from scratch in NumPy: from tensor strides and autograd graphs to BPE tokenization, multi-head attention, and INT8 quantization. It contains the programming tasks, unit tests, milestone challenges (Perceptron, XOR, TinyDigits MLP, CNN, Mini-Transformer, and MLPerf benchmarks), and `tito` CLI grading workflows.

2. **The Companion Textbook: *TinyTorch: From Tensors to Transformers***
   The full-length architectural commentary and systems textbook (available as `TinyTorch-Book.pdf` at [mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/)). While the Lab Guide provides exercises and stubs, the Textbook provides complete instructor solutions, formal systems invariants, execution traces, napkin-math memory and compute budgets, and production bridges to PyTorch and Triton.

Together, they accompany the broader [Machine Learning Systems](https://mlsysbook.ai) textbook (Volumes I & II) by Prof. Vijay Janapa Reddi at Harvard University.

## Curriculum Architecture

The 20 modules and 6 milestone projects progress through three progressive tiers:

- **Foundation Tier (Modules 01–08 & Milestones 01–03)**: Teaches core framework primitives—tensors, activations, linear layers, loss functions, data loading, reverse-mode autograd, optimizers (SGD, Adam, and AdamW), and the canonical training loop. Culminates in rebuilding the Perceptron (1958), resolving the XOR crisis (1969), and training an end-to-end MLP classifier.
- **Architecture Tier (Modules 09–13 & Milestones 04–05)**: Applies the engine to modern vision and language architectures—spatial convolutions (Conv2d, pooling), byte-pair encoding (BPE) tokenization, embedding tables, scaled dot-product causal attention, and full Transformer decoder blocks. Recreates the CNN revolution (1998) and the Transformer era (2017).
- **Optimization Tier (Modules 14–19 & Milestone 06)**: Transforms working implementations into high-performance systems—execution profiling, roofline modeling, affine INT8 post-training quantization, knowledge distillation, operator fusion, Key-Value (KV) caching, and rigorous benchmarking. Concludes with an MLPerf-style inference benchmark.
- **Capstone (Module 20: Torch Olympics)**: Synthesizes training, distillation, quantization, and KV-cached autoregressive inference into a complete deployable TinyGPT stack.

## How to Use This Guide

This PDF is compiled from the live interactive curriculum at [mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/](https://mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/).

- **In the Lab**: Use this guide alongside your code editor or Jupyter notebook. Install TinyTorch via `curl -sSL mlsysbook.ai/tinytorch/install.sh | bash` and use `tito module start <N>` to work through each module.
- **Online**: Visit the web version for interactive code runners in Binder and a per-module audio overview.
- **For Deep Architecture**: Consult the companion textbook, *TinyTorch: From Tensors to Transformers*, whenever you need to inspect full reference implementations, memory layouts, or hardware microarchitecture analysis.
